answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a single, non-transferable record of costly, verifiable work: an agent must complete attested tasks whose proofs accumulate slowly and cannot be copied to a new identity. Splitting effort across fakes leaves each history empty, like trying to fill a canyon with a spoon, while an honest record grows like a relic that gains value with age. Rewards are released only after peers attest the work, and the sweetest payouts, the nectar of the system, go to long, consistent histories, so cloning identities costs more than it can earn.
